subject: math

objective.text: Recognize the value of coins and count up to find their total value.

explanations.title: Coin values
explanations.text: A penny is 1 cent. A nickel is 5 cents. A dime is 10 cents. A quarter is 25 cents.

explanations.title: Count the same coin
explanations.text: Skip-count to find the value of the same coins. Count nickels by fives and dimes by tens. 5 plus 5 plus 5 equals 15 for 3 nickels.

explanations.title: Start with the largest coin
explanations.text: To count mixed coins, start with the coin of largest value. Count the dimes by tens first. Then add the ones.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: Counting the dimes first)

explanations.title: The cent sign
explanations.text: We write the value of coins with the cent sign. 23 cents is written 23¢. 100 cents can also be written $1.

explanations.title: Make a ten first
explanations.text: A quarter and a nickel make 30. Add the nickel to the quarter first. Then count on by tens and ones.

explanations.title: Decomposition tree
explanations.text: A decomposition tree breaks a whole into two parts. The two parts add up to the whole. 2 quarters make 50 cents, so each part is 25 cents.

examples.title: 2 dimes and 3 pennies
examples.text: Count the dimes first: 10, 20. Then the pennies: 21, 22, 23. The total is 23 cents.

examples.title: Quarter, nickel and penny
examples.text: 25 plus 5 equals 30. 30 plus 1 equals 31. The total is 31 cents.

examples.title: Make ten first
examples.text: 1 quarter, 3 dimes, 1 nickel, 2 pennies. 25 plus 5 is 30. Then 40, 50, 60. Then 61, 62. The total is 62 cents.
